title: The internet at the bottom of the sea
text: {{1}} is tempting to picture the internet as an airy cloud, but {{2}} reality it is a hard physical network: {{3}} the seabed run about five hundred fibre-optic cables, each {{4}} thick as a garden hose. Most failures are caused {{5}} ship anchors and trawling nets rather than by sharks, and when a line is cut, repair ships, {{6}} haul the cable to the surface, may need days to find the fault. In 2024, {{7}} several Red Sea cables were damaged in quick succession, engineers simply rerouted traffic through longer paths, and most users noticed nothing. Such resilience is the quiet achievement of the system: the cloud, {{8}} turns out, is held together by rope, glass and salt water.

gaps.hint: dummy subject: ___ is tempting to picture
gaps.explanation: 'It is tempting to…' — the dummy subject before the infinitive.
The cables lie across the seabed: across.

gaps.hint: adverb: each ___ thick as a garden hose
gaps.explanation: 'As thick as' — the first element of the comparison.

gaps.hint: relative: repair ships, ___ haul the cable
gaps.explanation: Non-defining relative after the comma referring to the ships.

gaps.hint: time relative: in 2024, ___ cables were damaged
gaps.explanation: Non-defining time clause after the year.
The fixed parenthetical phrase: 'it turns out'.
